skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed cloud media-analysis tool, but it also performs automatic identity setup, account login/registration, token persistence, and broad backend access with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads OpenClaw/Feishu identity environment variables and workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, writes a workspace data directory/database, and sends media or URLs to configured LifeEmergence backend APIs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, service, scheduler, or remote code execution mechanism was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though no explicit permission scope is declared.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly require automatic cloud history lookup and hidden internal identity handling, but they do not clearly require confirmation before uploading local media, forwarding URLs, or creating/logging into a backend account.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates or reuses a local SQLite sys_user record and can persist backend tokens/open tokens in plaintext; this is not system persistence, but it is sensitive local identity persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The frog-skin analysis purpose is coherent with media upload and cloud report retrieval, but the packaged common code adds generic API methods, account provisioning, user/token storage, and history access beyond the narrow visual-assessment workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with uploaded media or submitted URLs being processed by the configured cloud service, automatic backend identity creation/login, and local storage of user records and tokens. Prefer a version that documents network destinations, asks before uploads/history lookups, and limits token/database persistence.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially confirmed: network-backed analysis and history are disclosed, but silent phoneLogin registration, token handling, and broad common API/storage code are under-scoped for the stated purpose.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Partially confirmed: the top-level script sets the frog scene code, but the implementation is a generic cloud media-analysis client with report history rather than a constrained local frog-moisture analyzer.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed as a review concern: common helpers expose arbitrary HTTP methods, user lookup/storage, hidden open-id resolution, and remote URL forwarding that are broader than necessary.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed: the manifest does not declare a clear least-privilege permission boundary for shell invocation, file reads/writes, network destinations, identity data, or database persistence.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Confirmed in part: history lookup is a documented feature, but automatic cloud lookup on trigger phrases can access user-associated records without an explicit confirmation step.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed in part: local saves and cloud history are mentioned, but media upload, URL forwarding, account creation, and retention/token behavior are not clearly surfaced to users.
[YR4] expected: Overridden: manual inspection found a zero-width character in the description but no offensive tooling, exploit framework, or hidden malicious instruction.
[P9] expected: Overridden: the whitespace finding appears to be formatting in Python line wrapping; no concealed instructions were found.
[E1] unexpected: Confirmed as a review concern: the code can send the resolved local identity to a remote phoneLogin endpoint for silent registration/login.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G SARIF run reported no results; it did not independently substantiate a malicious classification.
